title: Part Four, Chapter 9: The Wonder-Working King Cucumatz

verses.t: And so the twenty-four lords and the twenty-four great houses were completed, when glory grew great in the Quiché, and the greatness of the Quiché's weight was exalted, and when the town was built of lime and stone; and all the peoples, great and small, who were in the charge of the lords came. And the glory of the Quiché was exalted when the house of the god and the houses of the lords were made. And it was not these who made them, nor did they labour, nor did they build their houses, nor did these build the house of the god; and so the vassals multiplied. And it was not by deceit, nor theft, nor plunder, for truly each of them belonged to the lords; and many were the kinsmen who gathered and crowded together to hear what each of the lords commanded. And all the lords were much loved and esteemed, and they were held in great esteem and veneration by all the vassals when the people of the town multiplied; and so, little by little, all the peoples and the enemies came to surrender. Nor were the peoples won in battle; rather they were exalted through the miracles of the lords. And King Cotuha, Cucumatz, was a worker of wonders: for seven days he would go up to the sky, and for seven days he would go down to the underworld; for seven days he would turn into a serpent, and truly he looked like a serpent; for seven days he would turn into an eagle, and another seven days into a jaguar, so that truly he was an eagle and a jaguar; and another seven days he would turn into clotted blood, so that he was only blood. And truly he was a wonder-working king, miraculous in his being, and he was a terror before all the lords. And this news spread, and all the lords and the peoples heard of the king's wonders. And this was the beginning of the greatness of the Quiché, when King Cucumatz made the signs of his greatness; and his line of sons and grandsons did not fail. And he did not do this because there was a wonder-working king, but to subdue the peoples, and to make it known that he alone was the head of all the peoples. And this King Cucumatz was of the fourth generation of kings, and he was also lord of the mat and the house, that is, of the throne; and he left descendants. And then he was exalted when he had sons, and he did many things; and Tepepul-Ztayul was begotten, and he was the fifth, and he reigned in the fifth generation. And likewise each of the lines of the lords had sons.
